I think the earlier failure came from the proof, not from the restatement. If `simp only` did not close the goal, Lean would have elaborated an error as `sorryAx`. The new proof avoids `simp` and uses the `decide` lemmas directly. I have not compiled this.

```json
{"mode":"iff","restated":"∀ language : BitLanguage, IsNP language = true → Nonempty (PromiseReduction language gapCVP400Promise)","proof":"unfold IsNPHardPromise\nexact ⟨fun h => of_decide_eq_true h, fun h => decide_eq_true h⟩","english":"For every language in NP (given as a Boolean predicate on bit strings), there is a polynomial-time many-one promise reduction from it to the GapCVP (gap n^(1/400)) promise problem: YES instances map to YES instances and NO instances map to NO instances.","why_clearer":"It removes the Bool-valued `decide` wrapper around classical decidability, so the statement reads directly as a universally quantified reduction claim."}
```

parsed.restated: ∀ language : BitLanguage, IsNP language = true → Nonempty (PromiseReduction language gapCVP400Promise)
parsed.proof:
unfold IsNPHardPromise
exact ⟨fun h => of_decide_eq_true h, fun h => decide_eq_true h⟩
parsed.english: For every language in NP (given as a Boolean predicate on bit strings), there is a polynomial-time many-one promise reduction from it to the GapCVP (gap n^(1/400)) promise problem: YES instances map to YES instances and NO instances map to NO instances.
parsed.why_clearer: It removes the Bool-valued `decide` wrapper around classical decidability, so the statement reads directly as a universally quantified reduction claim.
